LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 1.1.1 INTRODUCTION TO ORAL LITERATURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg
Topic 1.1: Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature, part of Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is oral literature important in the society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe genres of oral literature for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the features of oral literature from a variety of oral literature genres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. discuss the functions of oral literature for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of oral literature in daily life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or offline for the meaning of oral literature. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or offline for the meaning of oral literature. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.
2. listen to a recording on genres of oral literature and take notes. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials.
3. team up to prepare a visual organiser or mind map on the genres of oral literature and display in class.
4. summarise the features of oral literature.
5. peer review each other’s

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration are advanced as the learner engages in teamwork to research and share information

obtained from online and offline sources on the meaning of oral literature.

● Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner reflects on their own work when peer reviewing their work for correctness.

Values:
● Responsibility: Diligence is promoted as the learner searches for information online and offline.

● Unity: This is nurtured while the learner strives to achieve a common goal as they collaborate to prepare a visual

organiser.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues: This is nurtured as the learner cohesively works with peers as they search for information on oral

literature.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe genres of oral literature for information,
2. analyse the features of oral literature from a variety of oral literature genres,
3. discuss the functions of oral literature for comprehension,
4. appreciate the importance of oral literature in daily life.

Remember the key question: Why is oral literature important in the society?
